narrative: Material PL1__M933F308 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.442) with a mean of 896.61 units/day across 250 working days. Lead times are highly stable (CV=0.091, mean=0.942 days) after removing extreme outliers including a 31.97-day anomaly. The current SAP safety stock of 79 units is severely under-buffered relative to the statistically derived requirement of 645 units needed to achieve 95% service level. The EOQ of 2,793 units substantially exceeds the MOQ of 1,013, and the resulting max inventory of 3,438 units sits well within the 8,266-unit storage limit. Adopting the (r,Q) policy reduces total annual inventory costs by 22.5%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is largely continuous with moderate CV (0.442) and lead times are stable. The classical (r,Q) EOQ-based model with a z-score safety stock is well-suited: it minimises total ordering and holding costs while providing a closed-form reorder point that is straightforward to implement in SAP. No intermittency or high-variance lead time conditions exist that would necessitate a more complex (s,S) or base-stock model.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation is 41.6% (3,438 / 8,266 units) — ample headroom exists. No capacity constraint binds. If demand increases by more than ~140% the storage cap would become active.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1,013) and capacity (8,266) are fully compatible with the recommended policy (SS=645, Q=2,793, total=3,438)
